topics.title: Negative & conditional inversion
topics.summary: Inversión del sujeto tras adverbios negativos y en condicionales formales.
topics.theory:
**Inversión** = auxiliar + sujeto + verbo. Se usa en registro formal/escrito para dar énfasis.

**Tras adverbios negativos o restrictivos** (al inicio de frase):
- `Never / Rarely / Seldom / Hardly ever / Little / Nowhere`
- `Not only ... but also`, `No sooner ... than`, `Hardly/Scarcely ... when`
- `Under no circumstances`, `On no account`, `At no time`, `Only when / Only after / Only then / Only by`
- Si no hay auxiliar, se añade **do/does/did**: `Rarely does he complain.`

**Condicionales sin *if*:**
- `Should you need help, call me.` (= If you should need)
- `Were I you, I would accept.` (= If I were you)
- `Had we known, we would have left earlier.` (= If we had known)

**Ojo:** en `No sooner had I sat down than...` usamos **than** (no *when*); con `hardly/scarcely` usamos **when**. Tras `Not only` se invierte la primera cláusula, no la segunda. Con `So + adj` / `Such + be` también hay inversión: `So tired was she that...`
examples: Never have I seen such a spectacular view.
Not only did she win the award, but she also donated the prize money.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
Had I known about the delay, I would have taken the train.
Only after the results were published did people realise the scale of the problem.
commonMistakes: *Never I have seen this before -> Never have I seen this before.
*Not only she was late, but ... -> Not only was she late, but ...
*No sooner had he left when ... -> No sooner had he left than ...
*Rarely he goes out -> Rarely does he go out.
*Only when I arrived, I realised -> Only when I arrived did I realise.

topics.title: Cleft sentences (it / what / all)
topics.summary: Estructuras de hendidura para enfatizar información concreta.
topics.theory:
Las **cleft sentences** dividen una frase en dos partes para enfatizar un elemento.

**It-cleft:** `It + be + elemento enfatizado + that/who ...`
- `It was Maria who solved the problem.`
- `It was only after midnight that we got home.`

**Wh-cleft (pseudo-cleft):** `What + sujeto + verbo + be + elemento`
- `What I need is a long holiday.`
- `What she did was (to) complain to the manager.` (tras *do* el infinitivo puede llevar o no *to*)

**Reverse wh-cleft:** `A long holiday is what I need.`

**All-cleft:** `All I want is a bit of peace.` (= lo único que...)

**Otras:** `The reason why ... is that ...`; `The thing that annoys me is ...`; `The place where ...`.

**Cuidado:**
- Con persona usamos `who` o `that`; con cosas, `that` (no *which*).
- En it-cleft, el verbo *be* concuerda en tiempo con el contexto: `It was John that broke it.`
- Tras `The reason is` usamos `that` (no *because*): `The reason is that we lacked funds.`
examples: It was the lack of funding that caused the project to fail.
What really bothers me is the constant noise.
All I want is a quiet weekend.
It wasn't until 2019 that she moved abroad.
What we did was (to) book the tickets in advance.
The reason why he resigned was that he felt undervalued.
commonMistakes: *The reason is because ... -> The reason is that ...
*It was John which called me -> It was John who/that called me.
*What I need it is a rest -> What I need is a rest.
*It was yesterday when I saw him -> It was yesterday that I saw him.

topics.title: Mixed conditionals & alternatives to if
topics.summary: Condicionales mixtos y conectores alternativos a if.
topics.theory:
**Condicionales mixtos** combinan tiempos distintos:
- **Pasado -> presente:** `If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.` (if + past perfect, would + infinitivo)
- **Presente -> pasado:** `If she were more organised, she wouldn't have missed the flight.` (if + past simple, would have + pp)

**Alternativas a *if*:**
- `provided / providing (that)`: condición necesaria. `Provided that you pay in advance, we'll reserve it.`
- `as long as / so long as`: similar, más informal.
- `supposing / suppose (that)`: hipótesis. `Supposing you lost your job, what would you do?`
- `unless` = if ... not. `Unless you hurry, you'll miss it.` (no usar con *not*: *unless you don't*)
- `but for + nombre` = sin / de no ser por. `But for your help, I would have failed.`
- `otherwise` = si no, de lo contrario. `Leave now; otherwise you'll be late.`
- `in case` = por si acaso (no es condicional: `Take an umbrella in case it rains.`)
- `on condition that` (formal); `were it not for / had it not been for` (inversión).

**Error típico:** usar *will* tras `if/provided/unless` para futuro: `*if it will rain`.
examples: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Berlin now.
If he weren't so stubborn, he wouldn't have lost so many friends.
But for your support, the project would have collapsed.
We'll proceed provided that everyone agrees.
Supposing they refused, what would you do?
Had it not been for the storm, we would have arrived on time.
commonMistakes: *If it will rain, we stay -> If it rains, we'll stay.
*Unless you don't pay -> Unless you pay.
*I'll take an umbrella if it rains (por si acaso) -> ... in case it rains.
*But for you help -> But for your help.
*If I would have known -> If I had known.

topics.title: Wish / if only / it's (high) time / would rather
topics.summary: Deseos, arrepentimientos y preferencias con tiempos 'hacia atrás'.
topics.theory:
Se usa el **tiempo verbal "hacia atrás"** para hablar de situaciones irreales:

- **Presente irreal:** `I wish I had more time.` / `If only I knew the answer.` (past simple)
- **Pasado irreal (arrepentimiento):** `I wish I hadn't said that.` / `If only we had left earlier.` (past perfect)
- **Quejas/molestias sobre el futuro:** `I wish you would stop interrupting.` / `If only it would stop raining.` (wish + would; sujeto distinto, no se usa con *I wish I would*)
- Con **were** para todas las personas en registro formal: `I wish I were taller.`

**It's (high / about) time + past simple:** `It's high time you found a job.` (ya debería haber ocurrido)

**Would rather:**
- Mismo sujeto: `I'd rather stay at home.` (+ infinitivo sin *to*)
- Sujeto distinto, presente/futuro: `I'd rather you stayed.` (past simple)
- Sujeto distinto, pasado: `I'd rather you hadn't told her.`

**Otras:** `suppose/supposing`, `as if / as though + past` (`He talks as if he owned the place`).

**Error típico:** *I wish I would have*... -> `I wish I had`.
examples: I wish I had more free time to travel.
If only I had listened to your advice.
I wish you would stop leaving your clothes everywhere.
It's high time the government took action.
I'd rather you didn't smoke in here.
He behaves as if he were the boss.
commonMistakes: *I wish I would have studied -> I wish I had studied.
*It's time we go -> It's time we went.
*I'd rather you to stay -> I'd rather you stayed.
*I wish I will pass -> I hope I pass / I wish I could pass.
*I would rather to go -> I would rather go.

topics.title: Passive reporting structures
topics.summary: It is said that... / He is thought to...: pasivas impersonales.
topics.theory:
Los verbos de opinión o información (**say, think, believe, report, know, expect, consider, claim, suppose, understand, allege**) permiten dos pasivas:

**1. It + passive + that-clause** (impersonal):
- `It is said that the company is losing money.`
- `It was believed that he had fled.`

**2. Sujeto + passive + to-infinitive:**
- `The company is said to be losing money.` (infinitivo simple = mismo momento)
- `She is thought to have left the country.` (infinitivo perfecto = antes)
- `He is believed to be working abroad.` (infinitivo continuo = en curso)

**Reglas:**
- Si el hecho es anterior al verbo principal, usa **to have + pp**.
- Si el verbo principal está en pasado: `He was said to have been ill.`
- Muy usado en noticias y en writing formal para evitar atribuir la opinión a alguien concreto.
- Otros: `be rumoured/reputed/alleged`: `He is alleged to have stolen it.`

**Con *suppose*:** `be supposed to` suele significar obligación o expectativa: `You're supposed to arrive at 9.`

**Error típico:** *It is said to be that...* o usar *that* con sujeto personal + infinitivo.
examples: It is widely believed that the economy will recover next year.
The suspect is thought to have fled the country.
The building is reported to be on fire.
He is said to have been working on a new novel.
It was alleged that the minister had accepted bribes.
The new law is expected to come into force in March.
commonMistakes: *It is said to be that ... -> It is said that ...
*He is thought have left -> He is thought to have left.
*She is believed leaving -> She is believed to be leaving.
*People say he to be rich -> He is said to be rich.

exercises.prompt: The new bridge ___ to be the longest in Europe.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva impersonal: is said to be.

topics.title: Causative have/get
topics.summary: Have/get something done y have somebody do.
topics.theory:
La **causativa** indica que alguien hace algo **por nosotros** (o que algo nos pasa).

**have + objeto + participio:**
- `I had my car repaired.` (lo hizo otro)
- `She's having her hair cut tomorrow.`

**get + objeto + participio** (más informal): `I got my laptop fixed.` También para logros: `I finally got the report finished.`

**have + persona + infinitivo sin to:** `The teacher had us rewrite the essay.`
**get + persona + to-infinitivo:** `I got my brother to lend me his car.` (convencer)

**Experiencias desagradables:** `He had his wallet stolen.` (= le robaron). No hay intención, solo afecta al sujeto.

**Otros usos:**
- Negativo con **won't have**: `I won't have you talking to me like that.` (no lo toleraré)
- `have sb doing sth`: `She had us laughing all night.`
- `get sth done` también = completar: `We need to get this finished.`

**Errores típicos para hispanohablantes:**
- Decir *I repaired my car* cuando lo hizo otro.
- Olvidar el participio: *I had my hair to cut*.
- Usar *to* tras *have*: *had him to do it*.
examples: We're having the kitchen redesigned next month.
She had her handbag stolen on the train.
I'll get the mechanic to check the brakes.
The manager had everyone sign the new contract.
He got his essay marked by a native speaker.
I won't have you speaking to her like that.
commonMistakes: *I cut my hair yesterday (en la peluquería) -> I had my hair cut.
*I had my car to repair -> I had my car repaired.
*She had him to leave -> She had him leave.
*I got him do it -> I got him to do it.
*I have fixed my phone (por otro) -> I have had my phone fixed.

exercises.prompt: I need to ___ my passport renewed before the trip.
She got her brother ___ her with the move.
The teacher had the students ___ the exercise again.
He ___ his wallet stolen at the airport.

exercises.explanation: Experiencia desagradable con had + pp (broken into).

topics.title: Participle clauses (-ing, -ed, having + pp)
topics.summary: Oraciones de participio para escribir de forma más densa y formal.
topics.theory:
Las **participle clauses** acortan oraciones y dan estilo formal. El sujeto de la cláusula debe ser **el mismo** que el de la principal.

**-ing (activo, simultáneo o causa):**
- `Walking down the street, I bumped into an old friend.` (mientras caminaba)
- `Feeling tired, she went to bed early.` (causa)

**Having + pp (acción anterior):**
- `Having finished the report, he went home.` (= After he had finished)
- `Not having been informed, we missed the deadline.`

**-ed / being + pp (pasivo):**
- `Written in 1850, the novel is still popular.`
- `Faced with a difficult choice, she asked for advice.`

**Con conjunción:** `Before leaving, check the lights.` / `While waiting, we chatted.` / `Although exhausted, he kept going.`

**Dangling participle (error):** `*Walking down the street, the rain started.` (¿quién caminaba?) -> `Walking down the street, I got caught in the rain.`

**Otros:** `Generally speaking`, `Judging by`, `Considering that` son fijos y no exigen mismo sujeto.

**Error típico en español:** usar gerundio de posterioridad: `*He left, arriving at 8` es mejorable con *and arrived*.
examples: Having completed the course, she applied for a promotion.
Not knowing what to say, he remained silent.
Built in the 12th century, the castle attracts thousands of visitors.
Faced with mounting debts, the company went bankrupt.
Judging by the results, the campaign was a success.
Having been warned, they chose to ignore the advice.
commonMistakes: *Walking home, the rain began -> Walking home, I got caught in the rain.
*Having finished, the door was locked -> Having finished, she locked the door.
*Knowing not what to do -> Not knowing what to do.
*Before to leave -> Before leaving.
*Being a student, the library is useful -> Being a student, I find the library useful.

exercises.prompt: ___ the report, she emailed it to her manager.

exercises.explanation: El sujeto de la participle clause (I) debe coincidir.

topics.title: Relative clauses advanced
topics.summary: Whereby, in which, of whom, whose y comentarios con which.
topics.theory:
En C1 se usan relativas más formales y complejas.

**Preposición + whom/which** (formal): `The person to whom I spoke...` / `The report in which he explains...`
- Informal: `The person I spoke to.` (preposición al final)

**Cuantificador + of whom/which:** `She has three sons, two of whom are doctors.` / `Many books, most of which were old.`

**whose** (posesivo, personas y cosas): `A company whose profits fell...`

**whereby** = por el cual (sistema, acuerdo): `A system whereby citizens vote online.`

**Which-comment clauses** (se refieren a toda la oración anterior, con coma): `He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.`

**Defining vs non-defining:**
- Defining (sin comas, *that* permitido): `The book that I read...`
- Non-defining (con comas, nunca *that*): `My boss, who lives in Leeds, ...`

**Reducción:** `The man (who was) standing there...`

**Errores típicos:** *the man who I spoke to him*; usar *that* tras coma o tras preposición (*in that*); *what* como relativo (*the thing what*); omitir coma en non-defining. Tras *all, everything, something, anything*: `that`, no *which*: `everything that matters`.
examples: She has two brothers, both of whom work in finance.
The reasons for which he resigned remain unclear.
We introduced a policy whereby staff may work from home.
He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.
The author, whose latest novel won an award, will visit us.
The project, most of which was funded by the EU, ended last year.
commonMistakes: *The man who I spoke to him -> The man (who/that) I spoke to.
*All what he said -> All that he said.
*The book in that I found it -> The book in which I found it.
*My sister, that lives in Rome -> My sister, who lives in Rome.
*The people which live there -> The people who live there.

topics.title: Modal perfects & deduction
topics.summary: Must have, can't have, needn't have vs didn't need to.
topics.theory:
**Deducción sobre el pasado (modal + have + pp):**
- `must have` = casi seguro (afirmativa): `She must have missed the bus.`
- `can't / couldn't have` = imposible: `He can't have known.`
- `may / might / could have` = posible: `They might have left early.`
- `might not have`: `She might not have received it.` (*mustn't have* no se usa para deducción)

**Críticas y arrepentimiento:**
- `should have / ought to have` = deberías haberlo hecho (y no): `You should have called.`
- `shouldn't have`: `I shouldn't have said that.`
- `could have` = podría haberlo hecho (y no): `You could have told me!`

**needn't have vs didn't need to:**
- `I needn't have brought a coat.` (lo traje y no hacía falta)
- `I didn't need to bring a coat.` (no hacía falta; quizá lo traje, quizá no)

**Deducción con continuo:** `He must have been working all night.`

**Presente/futuro:** `must be`, `can't be`, `might be`.

**Errores:** *must to have*; *cannot have + past form*: `*can't have went`; confundir *must have* con *had to*: `had to` = obligación pasada; `must have` = deducción.
examples: She must have forgotten about the meeting.
He can't have finished already; it's only been ten minutes.
They might have taken a different route.
You should have told me you were ill.
I needn't have rushed; the train was late.
She must have been waiting for hours.
commonMistakes: *He must had left -> He must have left.
*She can't have went -> She can't have gone.
*I mustn't have forgotten (deducción) -> I can't have forgotten.
*You should told me -> You should have told me.
*I needn't to have gone -> I needn't have gone.

exercises.prompt: The lights are off. They ___ gone to bed.
exercises.explanation: Deducción afirmativa fuerte -> must have + pp.

exercises.prompt: He ___ have seen me; he walked right past without a word.
I took an umbrella but it didn't rain. I ___ it.

topics.title: Future forms advanced
topics.summary: Be about to, be due to, be on the verge of, future perfect y continuous.
topics.theory:
Más allá de *will* y *going to*:

- **be about to + inf:** inminente. `The film is about to start.`
- **be due to + inf:** previsto por horario. `The train is due to arrive at 6.`
- **be on the verge / brink of + -ing:** al borde de. `She's on the verge of resigning.`
- **be set to / be bound to / be likely to:** `They're set to win.` / `He's bound to complain.` (seguro)
- **be to + inf** (oficial): `The President is to visit Spain next week.`
- **Future continuous (will be + -ing):** acción en progreso en el futuro. `This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Rome.` También cortés: `Will you be using the car?`
- **Future perfect (will have + pp):** completada antes de un momento futuro. `By 2030 they will have built the bridge.`
- **Future perfect continuous:** duración hasta ese momento. `By June I'll have been working here for ten years.`
- **Present continuous** para planes: `We're meeting at six.`
- **Present simple** con horarios: `The exam starts at nine.`

**Tras conjunciones de tiempo no usamos will:** `when she arrives`, `as soon as I finish`, `by the time you get there`.

**Errores:** *when I will arrive*; confundir *be about to* con *be going to*.
examples: The plane is due to land at 14:30.
The government is on the verge of collapse.
By the time you read this, I will have left.
This time next week I'll be lying on a beach.
She is about to announce her retirement.
By next year, we will have been living here for a decade.
commonMistakes: *When I will arrive, I call you -> When I arrive, I'll call you.
*By next year I will live here ten years -> I will have been living here for ten years.
*I'm on the verge to cry -> on the verge of crying.
*The train is about arriving -> about to arrive.
*Will you using the car? -> Will you be using the car?

topics.title: Emphasis & fronting
topics.theory:
Para dar énfasis y estilo:

**Do-emphasis:** `I do like your idea.` / `She did warn us.` (con *do/does/did* + infinitivo, en afirmativa)

**So / such:**
- `so + adj/adv`: `so quickly`; `such + (a) + adj + nombre`: `such a beautiful day`.
- `so ... that` / `such ... that`: `It was such a hot day that we stayed in.`
- Con inversión: `So beautiful was the view that...` / `Such was the noise that...`

**Nor / neither / so + auxiliar + sujeto:**
- `She doesn't smoke, nor do I.` / `Neither can he.`
- `I love it, and so does she.`
- Con negativa: `I haven't seen it. Neither have they.`

**Fronting (colocar al inicio):**
- Complementos: `Gone are the days when...` / `Beside the river stood a church.`
- Objeto: `That I can't accept.`
- Locativos + inversión: `On the table lay a note.` / `Here comes the bus.`

**Otros énfasis:** `What's more`, `Not only that`, `at all` (`I didn't like it at all`), reflexivos (`I did it myself`), `ever` (`the best film ever`), `the very idea`.

**Errores:** *so a nice day* (-> such a nice day); *Neither I do* (-> Neither do I); *also not*.
examples: I do appreciate your help.
It was such a boring lecture that half the class fell asleep.
So heavy was the rain that the match was cancelled.
He doesn't speak French, nor does his wife.
On the hill stood an ancient castle.
Gone are the days when we could leave doors unlocked.
commonMistakes: *It was so a nice day -> It was such a nice day.
*Neither I do -> Neither do I.
*I like it too and also she -> and so does she.
*She did went -> She did go.
*So much noise it was -> Such was the noise.

topics.title: Concession & contrast linkers
topics.summary: Albeit, notwithstanding, whereas, even though, despite/in spite of.
topics.theory:
Conectores de **concesión y contraste** esenciales en writing C1:

- **although / even though / though** + cláusula: `Although it was raining, we went out.` (*even though* es más enfático; *though* también al final: `It's cheap. Not good, though.`)
- **despite / in spite of** + nombre / -ing / `the fact that`: `Despite the rain...` / `In spite of being tired...` / `Despite the fact that he was tired...` (no *despite of*)
- **whereas / while** = contraste entre dos hechos: `Sales rose, whereas profits fell.`
- **albeit** (formal) + adj/adv/frase: `a solution, albeit imperfect`
- **notwithstanding** (formal) + nombre: `Notwithstanding the risks, they proceeded.` Puede ir tras el nombre.
- **however / nevertheless / nonetheless / even so**: conectores entre frases, con coma.
- **much as / as much as** = aunque (formal): `Much as I admire her, I disagree.`
- **while / whilst**: `Whilst I agree, I...`
- **No matter how/what, however + adj**: `However hard he tried, he failed.`
- **Granted (that)** / **admittedly**.

**Puntuación:** `However,` va entre comas; *whereas* y *although* no llevan coma obligatoria tras ellos.

**Errores:** *Although... but...*; *in spite of that he was...* (bien: *in spite of that, he*) ; *despite of*; *although of*.
examples: Although the plan was risky, it paid off.
Despite having little experience, she got the job.
The first option is cheaper, whereas the second is more durable.
It was a good solution, albeit a temporary one.
Notwithstanding the objections, the proposal was approved.
Much as I respect her, I cannot agree.
commonMistakes: *Although he was tired, but he continued -> Although he was tired, he continued.
*Despite of the rain -> Despite the rain.
*In spite of he was ill -> In spite of being ill / the fact that he was ill.
*Even if he was rich he was unhappy -> Even though...
*However he is rich, ... (contraste) -> However, he is rich / However rich he is, ...

topics.title: Gerund vs infinitive with meaning change
topics.summary: Verbos que cambian de significado con -ing o to + infinitivo.
topics.theory:
Algunos verbos admiten ambas formas **con distinto significado**:

- **remember / forget + -ing** = recuerdo/olvido algo pasado: `I remember locking the door.`
  **+ to inf** = (no) hacer algo pendiente: `Remember to lock the door.`
- **stop + -ing** = dejar de hacer: `She stopped smoking.`
  **stop + to inf** = parar para hacer: `He stopped to buy water.`
- **regret + -ing** = lamentar haber hecho: `I regret telling her.`
  **regret + to inf** (formal) = lamentar comunicar: `We regret to inform you...`
- **try + -ing** = probar como experimento: `Try restarting it.`
  **try + to inf** = esforzarse: `I tried to open it but couldn't.`
- **go on + -ing** = continuar; **go on + to inf** = pasar a hacer otra cosa: `She went on to become a judge.`
- **mean + -ing** = implicar: `This means waiting.`; **mean + to inf** = tener intención: `I meant to call you.`
- **used to + inf** (hábito pasado) vs **be/get used to + -ing** (estar acostumbrado).
- **need + -ing** (pasivo): `The car needs washing.`; **need + to inf** (activo).
- **like/prefer:** `I like swimming` (disfrute) vs `I like to swim on Sundays` (hábito/costumbre).

**Siempre -ing:** enjoy, avoid, suggest, consider, admit, deny, risk, can't help, look forward to, be worth.
**Siempre to inf:** decide, manage, afford, refuse, hope, agree, fail, tend.

**Error típico:** *I look forward to see you* -> `to seeing`.
examples: I'll never forget meeting her for the first time.
Don't forget to submit the form before Friday.
He stopped to talk to a neighbour.
If the printer jams, try switching it off and on again.
She went on to win three Olympic medals.
I'm sorry; I never meant to hurt you.
commonMistakes: *I look forward to see you -> I look forward to seeing you.
*She stopped to smoke (dejó de fumar) -> She stopped smoking.
*I remember to post it yesterday -> I remember posting it.
*He suggested to go -> He suggested going.
*I'm used to wake up early -> I'm used to waking up early.

topics.title: Nominalisation & formal register
topics.summary: Convertir verbos y adjetivos en nombres para un estilo formal y denso.
topics.theory:
La **nominalización** transforma verbos/adjetivos en nombres para dar un tono académico y conciso.

**Verbo -> nombre:**
- `decide -> decision`, `develop -> development`, `fail -> failure`, `increase -> an increase`, `arrive -> arrival`, `grow -> growth`
- `Many people are unemployed` -> `Unemployment is a serious problem.`

**Adjetivo -> nombre:** `important -> importance`, `able -> ability`, `safe -> safety`.

**Ejemplo de transformación:**
- Informal: `Prices rose quickly, so people spent less.`
- Formal: `The rapid rise in prices led to a reduction in consumer spending.`

**Estructuras útiles:**
- `There has been a sharp increase in ...`
- `The growth of ... has led to ...`
- `A major factor contributing to ... is ...`
- `The introduction of ... resulted in ...`

**Otros rasgos formales:**
- Evitar contracciones y phrasal verbs: `investigate` (no look into), `postpone` (no put off).
- Pasivas y sujetos impersonales: `It can be argued that...`
- Verbos formales: `obtain, require, demonstrate, indicate`.
- Evitar `a lot of`, `get`, `things`.

**Error típico:** nominalizar en exceso hace el texto pesado. Usa un buen equilibrio y evita traducciones literales (*the people who live in the cities* -> `urban residents`).
examples: The introduction of a congestion charge led to a significant reduction in traffic.
There has been a steady increase in the number of remote workers.
Growing public awareness has prompted governments to act.
Failure to comply may result in a fine.
The unavailability of affordable housing is a major concern.
A key factor behind the decline is the lack of investment.
commonMistakes: *The people that live in cities -> Urban residents.
*Many persons are unemployed -> Unemployment is high.
*Look into / put off (en formal) -> investigate / postpone.
*The decision of government was say -> The government's decision.
*The increase of prices -> The increase in prices.

topics.title: Hedging & cautious language
topics.summary: Lenguaje prudente para evitar afirmaciones absolutas.
topics.theory:
En C1 conviene **matizar** las afirmaciones, sobre todo en essays y discusión.

**Verbos modales y semimodales:** `may, might, could, can be`; `tend to`, `appear to`, `seem to`
- `Young people tend to be more adaptable.`
- `The data appear to suggest a link.`

**It-structures:**
- `It would appear that...` / `It seems that...`
- `It is (generally) believed / widely accepted that...`
- `It could be argued that...`

**Adverbios:** `arguably, presumably, apparently, broadly, largely, to some extent, in many cases, generally, relatively, virtually`
- `This is arguably the most important factor.`

**Cuantificadores:** `some, many, most (no all)`, `a number of`, `in the majority of cases`.

**Otras fórmulas:** `To a certain degree`, `As far as I can tell`, `In my view`, `On the whole`, `Broadly speaking`, `There is evidence to suggest that...`, `This may well be due to...`.

**Cómo evitar generalizaciones:**
- `All teenagers are lazy.` -> `Many teenagers may appear less motivated.`
- `This proves that...` -> `This suggests / indicates that...`
- `Clearly/obviously` -> con cuidado.

**Error típico:** abusar de *always/never/everyone/nobody* y *proves*; mezclar *maybe* en essays (mejor *perhaps*, *possibly*).
examples: It would appear that the policy has had little effect.
Teenagers tend to spend more time online than adults.
This is arguably the most significant change in decades.
The results suggest that sleep may influence memory.
To some extent, the problem lies in poor planning.
There is evidence to suggest that exercise improves mood.
commonMistakes: *This proves that -> This suggests that.
*All young people are lazy -> Many young people may seem less motivated.
*Maybe the reason is ... (essay) -> Perhaps / It may be that...
*Everybody agrees that -> Most people agree that...
*The study shows definitely -> The study appears to show...

topics.title: Articles & countability errors (Spanish speakers)
topics.summary: Errores típicos con artículos y nombres incontables.
topics.theory:
Por influencia del español, los hispanohablantes cometen errores muy previsibles.

**Incontables (no plural, no *a/an*):** `information, advice, news, furniture, luggage, research, equipment, traffic, progress, knowledge, evidence, homework, weather, work, accommodation`
- *an information / informations* -> `a piece of information`
- `some advice`, `a piece of advice`, `much/little`.

**Artículo cero con generalizaciones:**
- `Life is hard.` / `Society needs change.` / `Education is important.` / `Women earn less than men.` (no *the life*, *the society*)
- `I love music.` pero `the music we heard last night` (específico).

**Usar *the* cuando es único o ya mencionado:** `the Internet`, `the government`, `the environment`, `the economy`.

**Sin artículo:** `go to school/university/hospital/work/bed/prison` (uso institucional); *go to the school* si es el edificio.

**Otros:** `in/at/on` + períodos; `the poor / the elderly` (adjetivo + the); `a/an` con profesiones (`She is a doctor`).

**Plural de ciertos nombres:** `the people are` (people es plural), `a police officer`, `the police are`.

**Errores de lista:** *the money don't*; *the news are*; *many informations*; *a travel* (-> a journey / a trip); *a work* (-> a job).

**Tip:** si en español dices «la sociedad» en general, en inglés suele ser `society`.
examples: Society should invest more in education.
She gave me some useful advice.
The news is better than expected.
Furniture is expensive in this city.
Could you give me a piece of information?
The government has promised to protect the environment.
commonMistakes: *Informations / an information -> information / a piece of information.
*The society is changing -> Society is changing.
*The life is hard -> Life is hard.
*The news are bad -> The news is bad.
*I need an advice -> I need some advice / a piece of advice.

topics.title: Collocations & dependent prepositions at C1
topics.summary: Colocaciones y preposiciones obligatorias en nivel avanzado.
topics.theory:
Memoriza bloques, no palabras sueltas.

**Verbo + preposición:**
- `depend on`, `rely on`, `result in / result from`, `lead to`, `contribute to`, `account for`, `apologise for`, `benefit from`, `focus on`, `object to`, `succeed in`, `consist of`, `cope with`, `comply with`
- `be aware of`, `be capable of`, `be responsible for`, `be accustomed to`, `be sceptical about`, `be reluctant to`, `be keen on`

**Colocaciones con *make/do/take/raise/give*:**
- `make a decision / progress / an effort / a mistake / a difference`
- `do research / damage / business / harm`
- `take into account / part in / advantage of / place / responsibility for`
- `raise awareness / concerns / questions / the issue`
- `give rise to / priority to / an example`
- `pose a threat / a problem`; `play a role / a part`; `conduct a survey`; `reach a conclusion`; `bear in mind`

**Adjetivo + nombre:** `heavy traffic, strong evidence, fierce competition, vital role, deep concern, widespread belief, major breakthrough`

**Nombre + preposición:** `an increase in`, `a solution to`, `a reason for`, `an effect on`, `a lack of`, `demand for`, `access to`, `a cause of`, `damage to`.

**Errores típicos:** *depend of*, *consist in* (por *of*), *the solution of the problem*, *interested of*, *marry with*, *discuss about* (no preposición), *emphasise on*.
examples: The outcome depends on a number of factors.
We must take into account the cost of living.
The campaign aims to raise awareness of mental health.
Heavy traffic is a major cause of air pollution.
She succeeded in persuading the committee.
The report highlights a lack of access to clean water.
commonMistakes: *depend of -> depend on
*discuss about -> discuss
*the solution of this problem -> the solution to this problem
*marry with -> marry
*consist in -> consist of

topics.title: Phrasal verbs & idioms useful for C1 speaking/writing
topics.summary: Phrasal verbs e idioms naturales para hablar y escribir con fluidez.
topics.theory:
Para el Speaking y el Writing, un pequeño repertorio bien usado vale más que muchas expresiones mal puestas.

**Phrasal verbs muy útiles:**
- `come up with` (idear), `put up with` (tolerar), `look into` (investigar), `carry out` (llevar a cabo), `bring about` (provocar), `set up` (fundar), `turn down` (rechazar), `cut down on` (reducir), `get away with` (salir impune), `back up` (apoyar), `point out` (señalar), `sum up` (resumir), `fall back on`, `catch on`, `phase out`, `make up for`, `live up to`.
- **Separables:** `turn the offer down` / `turn it down` (el pronombre va en medio). **Inseparables:** `look into the matter`.

**Idioms prácticos:**
- `on the whole` (en general), `by and large`, `to some extent`
- `a blessing in disguise`, `the tip of the iceberg`, `at the end of the day`, `a double-edged sword`, `once in a blue moon`, `in the long run`, `the last straw`, `a piece of cake`, `hit the nail on the head`, `break the ice`, `on the same page`, `a drop in the ocean`, `up in the air`

**Uso:** en Writing formal prefiere verbos formales (`investigate`, `reduce`); en Speaking mezcla ambos registros.

**Errores típicos:** romper el idiom (*the tip of the icebergs*), separar mal (*look the matter into*), usar *put up with* sin objeto, traducir literalmente (*it rains cats and dogs* se dice, pero no abuses).
examples: We need to come up with a creative solution.
I can't put up with the noise any longer.
The company plans to phase out plastic packaging.
It was a blessing in disguise; losing that job led me to a better one.
On the whole, the project went smoothly.
